sections.content: Real programs combine conditions: and/or/not logic, comparison chains, and sometimes a switch that maps many values to different actions.
Boolean algebra applies: conditions combine with AND (both true), OR (either true), NOT (flip). Parentheses control grouping.
Key points: keep conditions readable — extract complex logic into a well-named boolean variable instead of one giant expression.
